description: Ezekiel was told he only talks in riddles. When God asks you to speak, your job is to be faithful, not to make sure everyone understands.
excerpt: When God asks you to speak, your job isn't to make sure everyone understands. Your job is to be faithful with what He gave you. How it lands is between them and the Lord.
verse: "Then I said, 'O Sovereign Lord, they are saying of me, "He only talks in riddles!"'"
body_html:
Ezekiel is frustrated. He's been speaking what God told him to speak, and the people are brushing it off as riddles. They can't make sense of it, and they're mocking him for even trying.

Speaking for God can feel like that. What comes out of our mouths when we're actually sharing His words doesn't always land the way we hoped. Sometimes it sounds confusing to the people hearing it, or offensive, or like something they want to write off as weird and outdated.

The Bible says the words we speak can be the fragrance of life to some people and the fragrance of death to others. Same words, two completely different reactions, depending on where the heart of the listener is at. Jesus ran into this constantly. He'd say something packed with truth and half the crowd would get it while the other half would walk away angry. That's why He kept saying, let those who have ears, let them hear.

Ezekiel wasn't failing. He was being faithful. The issue wasn't how he said it. It was their willingness to hear.

Sometimes the reason we hold back from saying what God put on our heart is that we're afraid it's going to come out wrong, or that people are going to think we're one of those people. So we water it down. We keep it to ourselves. We tell ourselves we'll bring it up later when the timing's better.

But when God asks you to speak, your job isn't to make sure everyone understands. Your job is to be faithful with what He gave you. How it lands is between them and the Lord.

Where has fear of being misunderstood kept you from saying something God has been asking you to say?
question: Where has fear of being misunderstood kept you from saying something God has been asking you to say?
